stories.title: JLL’s Matt Landek to Lead New Data Center Operations Firm L5 Mission Critical
stories.excerpt: L5 Mission Critical, a new data center operations and management firm, has tapped Matt Landek as its first president and CEO. Landek previously spent 14 years at JLL, most recently serving as president of its data centers and critical environments division in Chicago. L5 Mission Critical, launched Wednesday by Detroit-based construction company Walbridge, was formed to meet growing demand for data center operations. From its headquarters in Chicago, L5 Mission Critical will offer operations, facilities management and workforce training to third-party data center clients across the U.S., as well as Walbridge construction clients. Landek will work alongside John Rakolta III, president and chief administrative officer of Walbridge. “Matt’s expertise will allow us to scale our data center construction practice to a full build-to-operate model that our clients need in this complicated time,” said Rakolta. “With the addition of L5 Mission Critical, our clients will be able to tap into a wider depth of service that goes across the entire life cycle of a data center.” Landek joined JLL in 2012 as an account executive, and was promoted to his most recent role overseeing employees across 340 data centers in late 2024, according to his LinkedIn profile. His time at the company coincided with the rapid expansion of the brokerage’s data center business. Prior to joining JLL, Landek worked in facilities management for the Cook County government in Illinois. He holds a degree in finance from the University of Illinois Chicago. A representative of JLL’s Chicago office could not be immediately reached for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Walbridge launches L5 Mission Critical data center ops firm, Chicago HQ, led by ex-JLL exec Matt Landek
New firm targets build-to-operate model for third-party data center clients nationwide
Growing demand for data center operations management drives full-service lifecycle offering
stories.summary: Walbridge Construction has launched L5 Mission Critical, a new data center operations and management firm headquartered in Chicago, with Matt Landek (14 years at JLL) as president and CEO. The firm will offer operations, facilities management, and workforce training to third-party data center operators and Walbridge construction clients. The move reflects Walbridge's strategy to scale its data center construction practice into a full build-to-operate service model.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, this signals sustained institutional capital confidence in data center development, which competes for land, financing, and construction labor in key metros like Chicago, Phoenix, and coastal markets; aggressive data center conversion of industrial and office inventory may limit available redevelopment sites and tighten contractor availability for apartment projects in competitive markets.

stories.title: Watch Brand Fossil Renews 15K-SF Showroom Lease at 366 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: A well-known watch brand is renewing its Midtown showroom, Commercial Observer has learned. Fossil, which sells affordable watches and accessories, has signed a renewal for the 14,786 square feet it occupies on the entire second floor of Joseph P. Day Realty’s 366 Fifth Avenue along East 35th Street, according to tenant broker CBRE. Asking rent and the length of the renewal were not immediately disclosed, but the average asking rent for Midtown office in the second quarter of 2026 was $86.18 per square foot, according to a report from CBRE. “This lease renewal highlights the enduring appeal of well-positioned showroom space along Fifth Avenue and underscores Fossil’s longstanding commitment to a location that has served its showroom operations for more than two decades,” CBRE’s Paul Walker, who negotiated on behalf of Fossil, said in a statement. “Fossil has occupied the space for approximately 25 years, making the location an integral part of the brand’s presence in New York’s accessory and fashion marketplace.” Michael Joseph and Aiden Campbell of Colliers represented the landlord in the transaction, but did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Other tenants in the building include fashion wholesaler Amiee Lynn, which also renewed its 29,000-square-foot lease in January and has been in the building since 2005, as well as leather goods wholesaler Mundi Westport Group, which took 10,800 square feet in April 2024. Fossil’s second-floor showroom sits atop Nature Republic, a Korea-based skin-care and makeup store. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fossil renews 14,786-SF showroom lease, 366 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan, 25-year occupancy
Midtown office asking rent Q2 2026: $86.18/SF; lease term and rate not disclosed
Retail anchor commitment signals stability on Fifth Avenue trophy retail corridor
stories.summary: Fossil has renewed its 14,786-square-foot showroom lease on the second floor of 366 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, where it has operated for approximately 25 years. The renewal was negotiated by CBRE's Paul Walker; terms were not disclosed, though Midtown office asking rents averaged $86.18 per square foot in Q2 2026. The lease underscores Fossil's long-term commitment to the Fifth Avenue location as a flagship presence in New York's fashion and accessory market.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Demonstrates sustained retail tenant stability in prime Manhattan office corridors, but does not affect apartment supply, demand, or capital availability in multifamily-focused submarkets.

stories.title: Thorofare Inks $35M Refi on Hardeeville Commerce Park
stories.excerpt: Thorofare Capital closed on a $35 million floating-rate senior mortgage loan for the cash-in refinance and lease-up of Gateway Commerce Park. The newly constructed, two-building Class A industrial warehouse and distribution facility totals 449,280 square feet and is located in Hardeeville, South Carolina, near the Port of Savannah. Thorofare provided a floating-rate, interest-only senior mortgage loan for the cash-in refinance and lease-up of Gateway Commerce Park. Completed in 2025, the flexible configurations can accommodate tenants ranging from approximately 36,000 to more than 330,000 square feet. The sponsor is actively marketing the property to warehouse and distribution users as it executes its lease-up strategy. The property is located less than 20 miles from the Port of Savannah, providing access to one of the largest container ports in the United States that houses North America’s largest single-terminal container facility. bullets: Thorofare Capital closes $35M floating-rate senior refi on Gateway Commerce Park, Hardeeville, SC
New 449,280-SF Class A two-building industrial, completed 2025, within 20 miles of Port of Savannah
Flexible configs (36K–330K SF) support lease-up strategy for warehouse and distribution tenants
stories.summary: Thorofare Capital arranged a $35 million floating-rate, interest-only senior mortgage for the cash-in refinance and lease-up of Gateway Commerce Park in Hardeeville, South Carolina. The newly constructed, 449,280-square-foot Class A industrial facility comprises two buildings with flexible configurations to accommodate tenants from 36,000 to 330,000 square feet and is positioned less than 20 miles from the Port of Savannah, a major container port.
stories.impact: Indirect but meaningful signal for Southeast multifamily markets, especially Charleston and Savannah metros: strong industrial real estate fundamentals and port-adjacent development activity drive logistics and distribution employment, anchoring population and wage growth in Lowcountry markets and supporting sustained apartment demand in satellite and emerging submarkets near the port and inland industrial nodes.

stories.title: Volta Global Acquires 110K-SF Hialeah Retail, Self-Storage Property
stories.excerpt: Volta Global landed a $17.35 million acquisition loan for Westland Plaza, a 110K square-foot mixed-use retail and self-storage center in Hialeah, Florida. JLL worked on behalf of Volta Global to secure a two-year, floating-rate acquisition loan through Shelter Growth Capital Partners (SGCP). Westland Plaza was built in 1979 and renovated in 2008. The site comprises of 50,000 square feet of retail across three buildings, along with a 60,000 square-foot, three-story self-storage facility. Notable tenants include Office Depot, Sherwin-Williams, Avis Budget and American Dollar Pharmacy. The property is located at 5301-5315 W 20th Ave. Nextdoor, Codina Partners is redeveloping the south-adjacent Westland Mall into a mixed-use community with more than 800 residential units. The property sits just east of the Palmetto Expressway, granting direct and nearby access to I-75, I-95, the Florida Turnpike, The JLL Capital Markets Debt Advisory team was led by Michael DiCosimo, Joshua Odessky and Miguel Pedersen. The post Volta Global Acquires 110K-SF Hialeah Retail, Self-Storage Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Volta Global acquires Westland Plaza, Hialeah, FL, $17.35M floating-rate acquisition loan, SGCP
110K SF mixed-use: 50K retail + 60K three-story self-storage, built 1979, renovated 2008
Adjacent Codina Partners redevelopment of Westland Mall will deliver 800+ residential units
stories.summary: Volta Global secured a $17.35 million, two-year floating-rate acquisition loan through Shelter Growth Capital Partners to purchase Westland Plaza, a 110,000-square-foot mixed-use retail and self-storage property in Hialeah, Florida. The property comprises 50,000 square feet of retail (anchored by Office Depot, Sherwin-Williams, Avis Budget, and American Dollar Pharmacy) and a 60,000-square-foot self-storage facility. Nextdoor, Codina Partners is redeveloping the adjacent Westland Mall into a mixed-use community with over 800 residential units.
stories.impact: High relevance for Miami-Dade multifamily: Codina's 800+ unit delivery at neighboring Westland Mall will drive competitive supply pressure in Hialeah and west Miami-Dade submarkets; the timing and financing accessibility suggest market absorption capacity, but new-build residential will likely compress rents on older apartment stock nearby; developers should monitor Westland Mall delivery pace and tenant mix to inform underwriting and positioning for value-add or ground-up projects in the corridor.

stories.title: Sagard Picks Up 400K-SF Fulton County Warehouse Facility
stories.excerpt: Sagard Real Estate acquired 5070 Phillip Lee Drive SW, a 400,800-square-foot industrial property in Atlanta’s Fulton Industrial submarket. SkyREM was the seller. The investment was made on behalf of Sagard Real Estate’s open-end core-plus real estate fund (the “Fund”). The property comprises four contiguous warehouse buildings across 15.5 acres along the Fulton Industrial Boulevard corridor. Located approximately two miles from Interstate 20 and four miles from Interstate 285, the site also provides access to downtown Atlanta and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. The property is fully leased to Kittrich, who manufactures and distributes rug underlays, non-slip products, bath mats, and related home goods. The tenant has occupied the property for more than 20 years. Existing demising walls and office configurations provide flexibility to accommodate multiple users over time. At the time of acquisition, no competitive warehouse product was under construction in the submarket, with the existing development pipeline designated for data center use. The post Sagard Picks Up 400K-SF Fulton County Warehouse Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sagard Real Estate acquires 5070 Phillip Lee Drive SW, Atlanta Fulton Industrial, 400,800 SF, $0 debt mentioned
Four contiguous warehouse buildings, 15.5 acres, fully leased 20+ years to Kittrich (home goods/rugs)
Zero competitive warehouse construction in submarket; existing pipeline designated for data centers
stories.summary: Sagard Real Estate acquired a 400,800-square-foot industrial property at 5070 Phillip Lee Drive SW in Atlanta's Fulton Industrial submarket on behalf of its core-plus real estate fund. The property comprises four contiguous warehouse buildings across 15.5 acres, fully leased to Kittrich for over 20 years, and is positioned two miles from I-20 and four miles from I-285. Notably, at acquisition, no competitive warehouse construction was underway in the submarket, with the existing development pipeline designated for data center use.
stories.impact: Significant for Atlanta multifamily developers: constrained warehouse supply pipeline and data center conversion of industrial inventory will tighten logistics employment hubs, potentially concentrating job growth in tech and distribution-adjacent sectors; this may shift wage growth and workforce composition in Atlanta, affecting demand demographics and rent-paying capacity in east and southeast Atlanta submarkets closer to Hartsfield-Jackson and industrial corridors.

stories.title: Redfearn Buys 24K-SF Delray Beach Retail Property for $1,640/Foot
stories.excerpt: Redfearn Capital paid $39.2 million for a 23,290 square foot retail and restaurant in Delray Beach. DHBH was the seller. The price comes out to $1,640 a square foot, one of the highest prices paid for a retail property in the area, according to Cushman & Wakefield, who brokered the deal. Cushman & Wakefield’s Mike Ciadella, Scott O’Donnell and Miguel Alcivar, along with Katalyst Real Estate’s Don Ginsburg and Adam Steinlauf, represented the seller. Cushman and Wakefield’s Florida EDSF Team, Ron Granite and Jason Hochman, represented Redfearn Capital in securing financing for the acquisition. “This acquisition gives us control of a landmark asset in one of South Florida’s most vibrant and supply constrained downtown markets,” said Alex Redfearn of Redfearn Capital. The properties at 105 and 111 E. Atlantic Ave. are anchored by a diversified tenant roster spanning established restaurant operators, office users, and on-site parking. The retail buildings were constructed in 1952 and 1971 on a 0.38-acre lot. The post Redfearn Buys 24K-SF Delray Beach Retail Property for $1,640/Foot appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Redfearn Capital acquires Delray Beach retail, 23,290 SF, $39.2M, $1,640/SF, one of highest area prices
105 and 111 E. Atlantic Ave., 1952 and 1971 construction, mixed restaurant/office/parking anchors
Buyer cites 'supply-constrained downtown market' and 'landmark asset' positioning
stories.summary: Redfearn Capital purchased a 23,290-square-foot retail and restaurant property in downtown Delray Beach for $39.2 million, or $1,640 per square foot—among the highest prices paid for retail in the area. The two buildings at 105 and 111 E. Atlantic Ave. were built in 1952 and 1971 on a 0.38-acre lot and are anchored by established restaurant operators, office tenants, and on-site parking. Redfearn characterized the acquisition as capturing a 'landmark asset' in one of South Florida's 'most vibrant and supply-constrained downtown markets.'
stories.impact: Signal of tight retail supply and strong investor demand in Delray Beach downtown, which may reflect spillover from compressed Miami rental market and gentrification pressure; rising downtown commercial valuations and retail scarcity often precede residential conversion or upzoning in historic cores, creating future multifamily development opportunities; monitor Delray Beach zoning changes and downtown redevelopment announcements for residential component potential in the South Florida Palm Beach County market.

stories.title: Inland Secures $112M for Chicagoland Senior Housing Portfolio
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged $112 million in acquisition financing from a regional bank for the purchase of a two-property portfolio of independent living, assisted living and memory care communities totaling 330 units in the Chicago area. JLL placed the financing on behalf of an affiliate of The Inland Real Estate Group, LLC. The JLL Seniors Housing Capital Markets team representing the borrower was led by Senior Director Sam Dylag. The stabilized portfolio consists of Deer Park Village, an 188-unit community in Deer Park that opened in 2016, and The Landings, a 142-unit community originally constructed in 2021 and located in Batavia. Dial Senior Living will continue management of the properties. “JLL has been a committed partner to our senior living investment strategy and delivered an attractive financing solution for this acquisition that expanded Inland’s lending relationships in a capital markets environment where experience and conviction matter,” said Joseph Binder, Chief Investment Officer of Inland. The post Inland Secures $112M for Chicagoland Senior Housing Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Inland Real Estate closes $112M acquisition financing for two-property Chicagoland senior housing portfolio, 330 units
Deer Park Village (188 units, opened 2016) + The Landings (142 units, 2021), Deer Park and Batavia, IL
Regional bank lender; Dial Senior Living continues management; JLL structured transaction
stories.summary: JLL arranged $112 million in acquisition financing from a regional bank for an Inland Real Estate affiliate to purchase a two-property senior housing portfolio totaling 330 units in the Chicago area. The portfolio comprises Deer Park Village, a 188-unit independent/assisted living community in Deer Park (opened 2016), and The Landings, a 142-unit community in Batavia (built 2021). Dial Senior Living will continue managing both stabilized properties.
stories.impact: Positive capital availability signal for Chicago-area senior housing and assisted living; however, limited direct impact on age-targeted multifamily (55+) or active-adult apartment development given senior housing is a distinct asset class with different financing, regulatory, and operational profiles; indicates regional lenders remain confident in Chicagoland demographics and demand for senior services, supporting overall regional multifamily capital markets confidence.

stories.title: U.S. Apartment Rents Decline for First Time in Eight Months: Report
stories.excerpt: Apartment rents in the U.S. declined slightly over the summer, particularly in August, but continue to grow on an annual basis, according to research from CoStar Group’s Apartments.com. The national average monthly rent fell 0.03 percent to $1,751 in August, a $1 decline from July’s upwardly revised level of $1,752, according to the data, ending a run of eight consecutive months of rent increases. “While apartment rent growth typically slows in the late summer leasing season, the 0.03 percent month-over-month decline recorded in August continues the recent pattern of late-summer rent decreases observed since 2024,” the report notes. But this August’s monthly decline was still “considerably milder” than the declines of 0.1 percent in August 2024 and 0.2 percent in August 2025, according to the report, suggesting an “improvement in pricing conditions.” GRAPHIC: Courtesy Apartments.com Still, rent growth around the country continues to climb on average despite elevated supply levels constraining pricing momentum, the report said. The Pacific Northwest and the Midwest led the charge in August, with both regions seeing the strongest year-over-year rent growth at 2.2 percent each. The Northeast’s 2 percent rise followed close behind. Overall, 12 of the top 50 markets posted month-over-month rent increases in August, while seven markets showed no change and 31 recorded declines. Some markets in California saw healthy monthly rent growth, with Orange County’s average rents up 0.6 percent, San Francisco at a 0.4 percent rise, East Bay rising 0.3 percent, and San Jose’s up 0.2 percent (the same as Chicago). On an annual basis, however, San Francisco was the standout, with an 11.9 percent year-over-year rent increase. bullets: U.S. apartment rents decline 0.03% YoY to $1,751/month in August 2024, first decline in 8 months
August decline 'considerably milder' vs. 0.1% (Aug 2024) and 0.2% (Aug 2025), signaling improvement
Annual rent growth continues despite elevated supply; Pacific Northwest and Midwest leading charge
stories.summary: According to CoStar Group's Apartments.com data, the national average apartment rent declined 0.03 percent in August to $1,751 per month, representing the first monthly decline in eight consecutive months of increases. The decline was notably milder than August declines in prior years (0.1% in August 2024, 0.2% in August 2025), suggesting stabilizing pricing conditions. Despite elevated supply nationwide, annual rent growth remains positive, with the Pacific Northwest and Midwest regions leading growth.
stories.impact: Critical market signal for all multifamily developers: supply normalization and month-over-month rent compression indicate demand-supply rebalancing and potential margin pressure on new deliveries; the milder decline vs. prior years suggests market has absorbed recent supply waves and rent declines are moderating, but elevated pipeline and continued deliveries in high-growth metros (Sunbelt, Pacific NW) will likely compress rents further; developers should focus on cost discipline, value-add repositioning, and markets with structural demand drivers (job growth, migration) rather than generic supply.

stories.title: Mesa West Lends $27M on Seattle-Area Apartments Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Timberlane Partners has secured $27 million of acquisition financing for the purchase of a multifamily complex in suburban Seattle, Commercial Observer has learned. Mesa West Capital supplied the five-year, nonrecourse, first-mortgage loan for Timberlane’s off-market acquisition and renovation of the Vista Ridge, a garden-style apartment community built in 1992 in Issaquah, Wash. Timberlane acquired the 91-unit property for $37 million earlier this month. “We believe Vista Ridge presents a compelling value-add opportunity with the vast majority of the property remaining in its original condition,” Josh Westerberg, head of Mesa West Capital’s west region, said in a statement. “Timberlane has a proven track record of successfully repositioning multifamily assets in the Seattle market and relied on our certainty of execution and ability to close quickly.” Westerberg led the loan’s origination out of Mesa West’s San Francisco office alongside JJ McMahon. The transaction closed in 23 days, according to the private lender. Located at 201 Mountain Park Boulevard SW 17 miles east of Downtown Seattle, Vista Ride consists of eight buildings with two- and three-bedroom units. Community amenities include a fitness center, covered parking, a swimming pool, a sauna, a clubhouse and a dog park. Timberlane Partners did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mesa West Capital arranges $27M five-year nonrecourse first mortgage for Timberlane Partners multifamily acquisition
Vista Ridge, Issaquah, WA, 91 units, garden-style 1992 vintage, acquired $37M, off-market value-add
Lender closed in 23 days; borrower has track record repositioning Seattle-market assets
stories.summary: Mesa West Capital provided a $27 million, five-year nonrecourse first-mortgage loan for Timberlane Partners' acquisition and renovation of Vista Ridge, a 91-unit garden-style apartment community built in 1992 in Issaquah, Washington. Timberlane acquired the off-market property for $37 million and plans extensive renovations, with most units in original condition. Mesa West closed the transaction in 23 days, underscoring quick turnaround for experienced sponsors with proven repositioning track records in the Seattle market.
stories.impact: Reflects strong capital availability and lender appetite for value-add multifamily acquisitions in Seattle metro; the 23-day close and $27M LTV ~73% indicates robust financing terms for seasoned operators with execution credibility; suggests Seattle market remains liquid and attractive for off-market deals despite elevated stock; developers with similar profiles should pursue value-add and repositioning opportunities in suburban Seattle (Issaquah, Bellevue, Redmond) where 1990s vintage assets present renovation arbitrage and market-rate uplift potential.

stories.title: The Plan: Fifth Avenue’s New Rolex Building, a Nod to Timelessness
stories.excerpt: Sleek, subtle, sophisticated, iconic: all accurate ways to describe a Rolex watch, and now also the Rolex Building at 665 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. The 30-story, 165,000-square-foot boutique Midtown office building replaced the 12-story structure built on the site in 1924. The new tower will open this fall, and will feature exteriors defined by a sculpted glass curtain wall, a vast amenity space, office space for a plethora of tenants — including Rolex, a tenant in and the owner of the old building — and a multifloor retail space, also for Rolex. “New York City, and Fifth Avenue in particular, have long been crucial to Rolex in the United States,” Luca Bernasconi, CEO of Rolex Watch U.S.A., said in a statement. “The Rolex Building at 665 Fifth Avenue is a clear expression of our enduring commitment to this city: a beautiful example of modern architecture that will serve our team and tenants, as well as welcome clients for decades to come.” The design of the building was formulated before COVID. The development phase occurred during the pandemic, and the topping-off took place last year, with third-party tenants slated to enter the building in early 2027. “The design of this building is incredibly intentional. It was designed in partnership with David Chipperfield, and the facades are inspired by the Rolex watch face,” Jonathan Fales, executive managing director at Cushman & Wakefield — which is handling leasing for the building — told Commercial Observer. “That is really the starting point with which the building can be viewed in a holistic way.” Building amenities will include a daytime food and beverage lounge with the option for al fresco dining on the 12th floor, as well as conference spaces plus a tenant-only restaurant on the top two floors. bullets: Rolex Building (655 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan) opens fall 2025, 30-story, 165K SF boutique office tower
Replaces 1924 12-story building; owner-occupied by Rolex + multifloor retail; trophy amenities, sustainability focus
Represents continued institutional capital and luxury brand investment in Fifth Avenue office
stories.summary: Rolex has completed development of a new 30-story, 165,000-square-foot boutique office building at 655 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, scheduled to open fall 2025. The tower replaces a 12-story structure built in 1924 and will house Rolex offices, multifloor Rolex retail, and third-party office tenants, along with amenity spaces including a 12th-floor food and beverage lounge with al fresco dining. The building emphasizes sustainability and premium workplace experience.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Signals continued trophy office investment and brand confidence in Midtown Manhattan despite secular office market challenges; however, conversion of Fifth Avenue office space to owner-occupied luxury showrooms reduces traditional office leasing supply and may support office-to-residential conversion opportunities in secondary Midtown locations as trophy corridors consolidate around marquee users; monitor broader Midtown office-to-residential rezoning trends for potential mixed-use development sites.
